record.final_answer:
Yes — it's already broken, not just at risk.

Corvane gateway 2.3 allows at most 5,000 parts per multipart upload (parts 8–512 MiB, last one exempt; 5 TiB per object). At 8 MiB that caps an object at 5,000 × 8 MiB ≈ 39 GiB. A 60 GiB tarball needs 7,680 parts, so the upload fails at the part limit — after pushing tens of GB.

Fix in scripts/upload.sh: CHUNK_MB 8 → 32 (scripts/upload.sh:10). That's 1,920 parts for 60 GiB, with headroom to ~156 GiB before you have to think about it again. 16 MiB would also work but only buys you to ~78 GiB. Keep it a multiple of 8 and never below 8 — 8 MiB is the documented floor, which is probably why it was picked originally.

Two things I couldn't check and you should confirm before relying on this:

- `corvane-cli` isn't installed here, so I couldn't verify it accepts `32MiB` in the same way or whether it has a concurrency flag. If it does, the part count also affects retry cost: one failed part is now 32 MiB to re-send instead of 8, which is the trade-off for the higher ceiling.
- The script has no retry or resume logic and no verification that the completed object matches the tarball size. A 60 GiB nightly upload with ~2,000 requests will occasionally lose one; worth adding `--retries` (if supported) and a post-upload size/ETag check.

If growth is unpredictable rather than slow, tell me and I'll make the part size computed from file size instead of hardcoded.
